before.title: Outgoing spherical trace and Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
before.statement: Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the complete normalised spherical harmonics of the spherical-harmonic lemma on $S_R$ ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version.
before.strategy: The boundary norm of the fractional Sobolev space is equivalent, for fixed $R$, to $\sum_{l,m}(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$: for finite harmonic data the harmonic ball extension $\sum(r/R)^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}$ has Dirichlet energy $\sum(l/R)|f_{lm}|^2$ by the first Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) and normal differentiation, and $L^2$ ball norm $\sum R/(2l+3)|f_{lm}|^2$ with the sphere-normalised basis, so its $H^1$ norm is equivalent to $\sum(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$. For arbitrary $H^{1/2}$ data the bounded right inverse and the weak harmonic Dirichlet solver of the prescribed-data lemma ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]) give a controlled harmonic $H^1$ extension; the harmonic coefficients and orthogonality of the ball Poisson series lemma ([[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]]) show the finite energy partial sums are bounded by its energy, giving both directions of the equivalence. The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. For the exterior realisation, define $u_{lm}(r)=f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)$, $r\ge R$; the finite polynomial positive formula gives $|h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)|\le R/r$ and, by the recurrence, geometric-in-$l$ radial ratios on every compact $r>R$ interval, so the series and all derivatives converge uniformly there, away from the sphere; the smoothness, the weak trace identification and the annular $H^1$ control follow from Green's identity for each mode on $[R,R+\delta]$ and the bounds above. Uniqueness: the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of $h_l(kr)$ and its incoming partner, whose Wronskian is nonzero; Sommerfeld selects $h_l$, and harmonic completeness forces any smooth outgoing exterior solution to have exactly this map.

after.title: Outgoing spherical trace and Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers. Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,Y_{lm}(n)$ with $Y_{lm}(n)$ in this radial display read as $Y^R_{lm}(Rn)$, is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion.

The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. before.title: Outgoing DtN coefficient at degree zero and the explicit PEC topology zero mode
before.statement: (i) At degree $l=0$ the outgoing radial function of the spherical Hankel lemma is $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$, so for $k,R>0$ the Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) is $t_0=kh_0'(kR)/h_0(kR)=ik-1/R$: its real part $-1/R$ is negative and its imaginary part $k$ is positive, as the spherical trace lemma requires. (ii) In the spherical shell $a<|x|<b$, the field $u(x)=\operatorname{grad}|x|^{-1}=-x/|x|^3$ is smooth on the closure, nonzero, normal to both boundary spheres, curl-free and divergence-free: $u=\nabla\Phi$ with $\Phi(x)=|x|^{-1}$ harmonic off the origin, so $\operatorname{curl}u=\operatorname{curl}\nabla\Phi=0$ and $\operatorname{div}u=\Delta\Phi=0$ there ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], [[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]). Thus $u$ lies in the PEC class $X$ of the cavity spectral lemma ([[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]) with zero curl, and it has zero curl eigenvalue: eliminating all topology zero modes would incorrectly discard this explicit admissible vector field.
before.strategy: (i) Direct computation: with $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$, logarithmic differentiation using the algebra of derivatives and the derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]) gives $h_0'(z)=h_0(z)\,(i-1/z)$, hence $kh_0'(kR)/h_0(kR)=ik-1/R$ with real part $-1/R<0$ and imaginary part $k>0$; both agree with the exact bounds of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). (ii) The field $-x/|x|^3$ equals the gradient of $-|x|^{-1}$ off the origin; the curl of a gradient vanishes ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]) and its divergence is the Laplacian of the fundamental solution, which vanishes off the pole ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]); on each boundary sphere $|x|=c$ the field $-x/c^3$ is a nonzero multiple of the outward normal, so its tangential part is zero and it belongs to the weak PEC class of the cavity lemma ([[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]); its curl is zero pointwise, so it is a nonzero vector in the kernel of the curl form, and such a vector is exactly a zero eigenvalue solution that any complete spectral description of the PEC class must retain.

before.title: Well-posed weak solvability and classical regularity for declared smooth-domain elliptic boundary problems
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability lemmas. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] is the local graph definition used throughout), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive ($\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ on $\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$), and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. Then:
(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ pointwise with $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.
(b) **Neumann.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ satisfying the compatibility condition $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,dS=\int_\Omegaho\,dx$ there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$, unique up to an additive constant; the normalised solution with $\int_\Omega u=0$ is unique and is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$.
(c) **Transmission.** For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$ on the interfaces, the corresponding weak transmission problem has exactly one globally $H^1$ solution with equal one-sided traces; it is $C^\infty$ on each closed side, and where the classical derivatives exist the jump of the flux satisfies $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]].
Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this item states the combined existence-and-regularity theorem on the declared domains.
before.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Necessity of compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis)

after.title: Well-posed weak solvability and classical regularity for declared smooth-domain elliptic boundary problems
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability lemmas. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] is the local graph definition used throughout), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive ($\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ on $\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$), and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. Then:
(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ pointwise with $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.
(b) **Neumann.** For every smooth outward conormal datum $g$ satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$, there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$. It is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ for each component gives a unique normalised solution, smooth on each closed component. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$, with a single additive constant.
(c) **Transmission.** For the stated finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth bulk $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b). The weak right-hand side includes $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$ and, in the Neumann case, $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique. With outer Neumann data it exists exactly when the total right-hand side vanishes on the constant of each connected component, equivalently $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for each $j$, and is unique modulo componentwise constants; zero componentwise means give uniqueness. In either case the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]].
Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this item states the combined existence-and-regularity theorem on the declared domains.
after.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Testing the displayed weak identity with the constant on each component gives $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, including the minus sign when solved for the outer conormal integral. Necessity of componentwise compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) Apply the transmission functional including the sheet-charge term, with outer Dirichlet tests in $H_0^1$ for full uniqueness, or outer Neumann tests in $H^1$ with that functional zero on every componentwise constant and the chosen mean normalisation. The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.

before.title: Uniqueness of the outgoing scalar Helmholtz solution with a smooth obstacle
before.statement: Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Suppose $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$ with the Euclidean Laplacian $\Delta$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), vanishes on $\partial O$, and is outgoing in the class of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: its trace $f=u|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ is $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense of that lemma. Then $u=0$ on $D$. No decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated outgoing class is assumed.
before.strategy: Green's identity on the truncated exterior. Apply the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] to $u$ and its complex conjugate on the bounded $C^1$ domain $D\cap B_R$, whose boundary consists of $\partial O$ and $S_R$: the volume integral is the real number $\int_{D\cap B_R}(|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2)\,dx$, and the inner boundary contributes zero because $u=0$ on $\partial O$. The boundary pairing on $S_R$ is therefore the real part of the DtN pairing, so $\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=0$. By [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]] applied to $f$ the imaginary part is $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$; taking real and imaginary parts of the identity $\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle+i\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=0$ gives both pairings zero, hence every coefficient $f_{lm}=0$. Consequently the outgoing exterior series of that lemma, which is the unique outgoing finite-energy solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$, vanishes on $\{r>R\}$; combined with $u=0$ on $\partial O$ the function $u$ vanishes on the complement of $D\cap\overline B_R$. Propagation. On $D$ the real and imaginary parts of $u$ are $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solutions of $\Delta w=Vw$ with the bounded coefficient $V=-k^2$, so [[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]] applies to each of them on the connected open $D$: each vanishes on the nonempty open set $D\cap\{r>R\}$, hence on $D$. Therefore $u=0$ on $D$. No finite experimental observation or physical postulate is used.

before.title: Existence and uniqueness for the smooth exterior vector Helmholtz mixed boundary problem
before.statement:

Zero Neumann transmission data admit all constants until componentwise normalization.
Green volume is real so only imaginary DtN pairing vanishes; strict positivity suffices.
